synopsis: General aviation pilot executed a go-around while entering the traffic pattern.  An uncontrolled field with heavy traffic.
EMB-145 Captain took issue with the VFR corridor below the Runway 4R approach path at JFK. The VFR traffic at 500 feet causes a TCAS RA with the EMB145 passing over at 900 feet.
GA pilot reported a NMAC twice with an aircraft in the pattern.
PRC Ground Controller and pilots reported a runway incursion. Aircraft was initially told to hold short; but they read back cross which was not corrected by ATC.
Reporter describes confusing taxiway markings that may lead to a runway incursion.
Pilot reported an NMAC in the traffic pattern at a non-towered airport.
Pilot reported that a Tower Controller instructed them to line up and wait while clearing another aircraft to takeoff on the same runway; resulting in a ground conflict.

An air carrier crew missed the CYUL Runway 06 LASHO line on Runway 10/28 because they did not recognize the thin yellow line as a LASHO line and also did not receive the NOTAM indicating Runway 10/28 was being used as a taxiway.
A319 Captain experiences a Green Hydraulic System failure at FL350 preceded by brake faults and nose wheel steering faults. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport.
M20 pilot reported experiencing an NMAC in the pattern at FIT airport.

An 'O' ring on a DHC8-300's Number Two Hydraulic system failed in flight causing the loss of all hydraulic fluid and system pressure so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
B737 flight crew leveling at 8;000 FT experiences a TCAS RA due to VFR traffic at 8;500 FT and descends.
ZHU described a conflict event when an Air Carrier accepted a climb clearance intended for another aircraft; the Controller acknowledging his/her failure to issue a similar call sign warning.
Flight Instructor reported an NMAC event during traffic pattern training due to inaccurate communication and pattern entry by the conflict aircraft.
Pilot reports of confusion while taxiing about hold short bars that he isn't sure if he should cross or not.
Instructor reported an NMAC with a banner towing aircraft in the traffic pattern.

A Gulfstream 200 flight crew declared an emergency and diverted due to right hydraulic system failure. Diverted again when their original diversion airport had inadequate runway length due to construction.

A flight instructor and private pilot reported a loss of engine power after takeoff in a M20; resulting in an off-field landing. Reportedly the fuel selector was inadvertently placed in position for the tank with minimal fuel.
Medium Large transport flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on the approach to CID. They discovered they had the wrong altimeter setting entered.
Pilot reported an NMAC event during landing with a non reporting aircraft in traffic pattern.
Captain reported encountering an NMAC event with another aircraft during initial approach.

B737 flight crew reported being cleared to climb via the ORCKA1 except maintain 15;000 feet. Level at 15;000 feet; the next Controller issued a climb via SID clearance which confused the crew and they remained at 15;000 feet while ATC intended them to the top altitude on the SID.
B767-300 Captain reported a Resolution Advisory on approach to land.
Piper J3 Cub pilot reported an NMAC at an uncontrolled airport requiring evasive action.

Phenom 300 Captain experienced a TCAS RA and NMAC at 6000 feet during vectors for approach. A VFR Cessna climbing to 5500 feet with the same Controller had continued to climb resulting in evasive action and a NMAC.
C-182 pilot reported landing on a highway after the engine quit because of fuel starvation.
CRJ-900 flight crew reported descending below cleared altitude on approach to MKE due to distractions; workload; and failure to follow SOP.
Falcon 900 Captain reported responding to a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb; avoiding another aircraft that was only detected by the TCAS system for a matter of seconds.
B737 flight crew reported IAS and Altitude DISAGREE annunciators at cruise altitude. On descent; the indications agreed and were verified by ATC.

B737-700 Fligt Crew reports being cleared to 'Climb via SID; except maintain 17;000 feet'. The First Officer read back; 'climb unrestricted to 17;000' and was not corrected. The crossing restriction at ARILE was not clomplied with.
A hearback\readback breakdown in communication between a B777 flight crew and ATC resulted in a temporary track deviation in the Middle East.

Pilot describes a situation where they are in a descent and get a RA at the same time the Controller issues traffic.  They descend as the RA suggests and turn to a heading issued by the Controller.  Traffic is not seen but suggested to be a drone by the pilot.
B737 flight crew reported that a combination of poor lighting; construction; and lack of signage made it extremely difficult to discern the correct path into the ramp.

A Cessna C-162 aircraft non-flying pilot reports how the lack of a clear read-back by the pilot flying to a Tower Controller for runway crossing clearance contributed to a near miss with another aircraft taking off. Snow piled high on side of runway completely blocking vision from taxiway also a factor.
Air Carrier Captain taxiing for departure from PHL reported confusing taxiway signage.

Two aircraft on downwind to CTAF U42 had a near miss after one pilot in the pattern turned downwind early to avoid Class B and may not have made a downwind call in accordance with Advisory Circular 90.66 or the other pilot entering the pattern downwind did not hear the downwind call.
B777 First Officer reported returning to departure airport following the loss of pressure and fluid in the left hydraulic system.
An aircraft on final had to execute a go around when an M20 pilot; unfamiliar with the airport and uncomfortable with radio communications; inadvertently crossed the runway hold short lines.
Air carrier flight crew reported being high on the approach due to task saturation; communications errors and focusing outside for traffic.

A Maintenance Controller reports how miscommunication and misunderstanding between himself and a B737-700 flight crew led to a takeoff departure with both Engine Electronic Controls (EEC) in the Alternate Mode. Number 2 Engine Control Light had illuminated after pushback.
B737-700 First Officer reported failure of Engine Driven Hydraulic System A. They declared an emergency and diverted to a suitable nearby airport for a safe landing.

A B757 Captain rejected the takeoff because the First Officer's airspeed indicator was malfunctioning. The previous flight had the same malfunction which the Captain briefed the First Officer about prior to the flight.
B737 First Officer reported experiencing an aircraft critical equipment failure requiring a diversion to a suitable airport. Flight landed without incident.
Air carrier Captain reported having trouble reading the airport taxiway signs due to high grass at IAH.
After returning to departure airport with unreliable airspeed indication; the Captain suggested moving necessary charts to the relevant portion of the QRH for ease in location and use.
A general aviation pilot reported directional taxiway signage at Tullahoma Regional Airport is not accurate and could lead to turning onto the incorrect runway.

A pilot and instructor were in the flare for landing when they spotted another aircraft on approach to the opposite direction runway. They took evasive action and the other aircraft landed normally. They also landed normally after a circuit around the pattern.
B737-8 flight crew reported unreliable airspeed indications during heavy precipitation.
B737-800 First Officer reported unreliable airspeed indications on Captain's side during arrival descent.
DVT Tower Controller reported an unsafe situation with a departure and an aircraft that needed to cross the runway.
B737-700 flight crew reported airborne conflict and a TCAS TA in climb to FL380. Captain speculated either ATC error or readback/hearback contributed to the event.

The flight crew of a CRJ200 taxiing for takeoff mistook a line up and wait clearance intended for another flight coming from the opposite side of the runway as being for them and entered the runway without a clearance. A prior query from ATC asking if they would be 'ready at the end' was cited as a contributing factor to their assumption of the clearance.

Two pilots report about fuel leaking from the most Aft Drain Mast on three CRJ-700 aircraft that have been deferred under a company Time Deferral that would not be allowed under an MEL or CDL deferral.

MD11 Captain reports getting low during a visual approach in hazy conditions with the autopilot engaged and ostensibly programed to fly the GPS RNAV approach. Vertical speed had been used for descent and PROF had not been reengaged to follow the vertical path.
SEE Ground Controller reported a runway incursion attributed to aircraft taxiing to different FBO's for cheaper gas prices on the airport.
ERJ145 Captain reported that a hydraulic system failure resulted in a diversion.

A319 flight crew reports a HYD G RSVR OVHT ECAM during climbout and complies with ECAM actions; turning off the green engine driven pump and the PTU.  Upon doing so a strong vibration is felt in the airframe and through the flight controls.  Attempts to quell the vibration are initially unsuccessful and the decision is made to divert.  The vibration continues and the crew elects to turn the green hydraulic system pumps back on since the overheat had gone away.  This action has a positive effect and a normal landing ensues at the diversion airport.
MD-11 Captain reported his airspeed indicator became unreliable; possibly due to pitot icing.

CRJ-900 flight crew reports missing a crossing restriction at STONZ on the BRDJE1 RNAV arrival to DFW. The minimum altitude on the arrival of 8000 feet was set in the MCP and the vertical speed was being controlled via the autopilot; as the aircraft has no VNAV capability.
Flight Crew reported airspeed indications became unreliable at cruise so they descended and airspeed returned to normal.
Air Carrier Captain reported responding to a RA; making evasive manuever; while level at 10;000 ft.

A Captain and First Officer return to a departure airport after noticing the Number 2 Hydraulic Quantity was down to one quart on their DHC-8-100 aircraft and no caution lights had illuminated. After Normal Gear Extension the Number 2 Hydraulic Quantity went to .7; Caution lights illuminated. Maintenance noticed a hydraulic flex line had failed in the Nose wheel well; even though the line was still within duty cycle limitations.

Both EMB-145 airspeed indications became unreliable during the descent initiation from FL360 so the Unreliable Airspeed procedure was accomplished. Airspeed indication returned to normal around FL290 and frozen moisture in the pitot system plumbing beyond the pitot tubes is suspected.
B737 MAX 8 flight crew reported unreliable airspeed fluctuations during icing conditions.
CRJ Captain reported as they entered the runway to depart a non-towered airport they observed an aircraft taking off from the opposite direction.
B757 Captain reported discovering after the flight that all three altimeters were incorrectly set by one inch of mercury when they flew the PURRL2 RNAV arrival to DEN.
Corporate Captain reported nonstandard procedures were used causing an attitude deviation. Captain stated lack of flying due to the COVID-19 pandemic was a contributing factor.
Pilots report of taxiing to a runway but crossing a closed runway in the process at LAX.
An air carrier Captain advised the Taxiway signage at CHS is inadequate and could be hazardous under low visibility conditions.
When a B737-700 flight crew responded as directed to a TCAS RA Center advised their required compliance with the TCAS commands may have resulted in a deviation.
Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing a taxiway incursion at LGA airport.  The crew cited experience and confusing ATC instructions as contributing factors.
MD-82 Captain reported receiving a Resolution Advisory (RA) on a 'descend via' clearance; citing workload in the old technology transports as interfering with their traffic scan.

A Citation pilot departing on a flight from FAT to SMF understood his clearance to depart Runway 29L at FAT; proceed direct LINDN; direct SAC; direct.  After takeoff when; to Departure's surprise; he started the sharp left turn direct to LINDN intersection; 200NM south of FAT; Departure and the reporter realized the intended fix pronounced 'linden' was the LIN VOR 100NM north of FAT well on the way to his destination; not the airways fix LINDN just north of Los Angeles.
CRJ-900 flight crew reported they descended below the level off altitude when the autopilot did not capture.
B737 flight crew reported the Captain's airspeed indicator became unreliable and control was transferred to the First Officer.
